subject: Availability cadence and monthly service-credit structure for Veridian pilot
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@veridian.io>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify standard uptime % and monthly credit cadence for pilot

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profile. Before we move to signature we need to confirm a few SLA mechanics for the pilot so our procurement and SRE teams can sign off:

- What is Redwood's standard availability baseline you expect to ship in the hosted offering (we need the explicit uptime % for the template)?
- How are monthly service credits measured and paid (monthly accrual vs single payout)?
- Is there a hard cap on credits per month (percentage of invoice)?
- Do you have standard carveouts for scheduled maintenance or batched-inference degradation?

I attached our internal SLA checklist as context. Looking for a concise answer so I can route to finance/legal.

Best,
Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Cloud Ops, Veridian Systems
elena.torres@veridian.io
ops@veridian.io

Attachments: Veridian_SLA_Checklist.xlsx (referenced)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@veridian.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 10:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify standard uptime % and monthly credit cadence for pilot

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Internal note: looping Laura (GTME) and Ben (Pricing/Contracts) to expedite.

Quick answers up front, then a proposed pilot-specific carve: 

1) Baseline uptime: Redwood's standard hosted baseline is 99.95% monthly availability for production-tenants. That is our public template for hosted API customers.

2) Monthly service credits: credits are measured and accrued monthly against verified availability windows. Credits are applied as a credit to the next invoice (we do not issue cash payouts for contractual credits). They accrue each month and are reconciled on the subsequent invoice cycle.

3) Monthly cap: Standard template sets a cap of 30% of the monthly invoice for a given month (to limit systemic exposure). For the Veridian pilot we can propose a narrower cap based on your usage profile — see proposed matrix attached.

4) Carveouts: scheduled maintenance (>=48h notice for planned maintenance affecting <1% of your routed capacity), operator-initiated scaling events, and documented batched-inference backfills are treated as carveouts in the template. We do allow for one small burst-exemption per quarter for short degradation during expected traffic migrations.

Proposed pilot exception (to make the contract motion faster):
- Pilot uptime anchor: 99.90% for first 90 days (so you get fast time-to-value while we tune prefix caching/quant profiles)
- Credit cadence: monthly accrual, paid as invoice credit next billing cycle
- Pilot monthly cap: 30% standard, but as a negotiation point we can consider 25% if Veridian commits to a 3‑month usage minimum (details in the attached monthly-credit-matrix.xlsx)
- SLA exclusions: agreed scheduled maintenance + batched inference carveout; emergency maintenance excluded from credit triggers if Redwood provides a technical incident report within 72 hours.

I've attached: Veridian_SLA_Draft_v3.pdf (redline of our template) and monthly-credit-matrix.xlsx with a few scenarios. Ben/Laura — can you flag any legal/finance blockers?

Cheers,
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Partnerships — Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Phone: +1 415 555 0123

Attachments: Veridian_SLA_Draft_v3.pdf, monthly-credit-matrix.xlsx
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@veridian.io>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify standard uptime % and monthly credit cadence for pilot

Sergio — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Quick responses from our side: 

- 99.90% pilot anchor is acceptable for the 90-day tuning window.
- Monthly accrual with invoice credit is fine.
- We would prefer the pilot monthly cap to be 25% (not 30%) given the pilot scope; Veridian is prepared to commit to a 3-month minimum.
- Emergency maintenance carveout is OK if the 72-hour incident report commitment is included in the contract.

I attached a brief redline with the 25% cap and the 72-hour report clause. If Redwood can accept those two edits we can route to our commercial contracts team for a quick signature.

Thanks — Elena

Subject: Next steps — Veridian pilot SLA redline

All,

Thanks team — Veridian has accepted the 99.90% pilot anchor and asked to move the pilot cap to 25% with a 3-month commitment and the 72-hour incident report clause. That aligns to what Sergio suggested but changes the cap from 30% to 25%.

Action items:
- Ben: can the finance team accept a 25% pilot cap for a 3-month committed pilot? Please flag any billing or accounting requirements.
- Ben/Legal: take the attached veridian-sla-redline.docx and produce a contract-ready redline. Priority: include the 72-hour incident-report SLT and clarify scheduled maintenance notice window (we currently state >=48 hours).
- Sergio: I'll prep a short summary for the Veridian commercial contract lead once Ben signs off.

Let's aim to have a contract-ready redline by end of day Friday so Veridian can route to commercial legal early next week. HubSpot deal link below.
